text: The boys followed the trail. <break time="0.8s" /> And found places. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the moose had turned. <break time="0.8s" /> And fought hard against the wolves. <break time="0.8s" /> At last they crept through the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> And quietly pushed aside. <break time="0.8s" /> The branches of a spruce tree. <break time="0.8s" /> To watch. <break time="0.8s" /> The old moose was tired and wounded. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet it kept tossing its great horns. <break time="0.8s" /> At the gray wolves. <break time="0.8s" /> Until the very end. <break time="0.8s" /> Koskoosh came back from his memories. <break time="0.8s" /> And found the fire almost out. <break time="0.8s" /> So he put more sticks on it. <break time="0.8s" /> From the small pile. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a long howl. <break time="0.8s" /> Sounded close by and a cold nose. <break time="0.8s" /> Touched his cheek. <break time="0.8s" /> He waved a burning stick. <break time="0.8s" /> And the wolves drew back. <break time="0.8s" /> But they did not go far. <break time="0.8s" /> And he heard them moving. <break time="0.8s" /> In a circle around him. <break time="0.8s" /> In his mind. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw the old moose again. <break time="0.8s" /> Standing alone in the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> While the gray wolves came closer. <break time="0.8s" /> Why should he hold on to life. <break time="0.8s" /> Koskoosh asked himself. <break time="0.8s" /> When it was the law. <break time="0.8s" /> That every life must end. <break time="0.8s" /> He let the burning stick fall. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> Where its little flame quietly went out. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, as the circle of wolves closed in he bowed his head and thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Is it not the law of life.
